g.title: C10
g.text: high SIL, compute the same function and
must agree. Channel b receives the owner's
result, compares it with its own, and
returns the verdict to the owner over an
edge with one initial token; on a
disagreement the owner marks its output
invalid and the pair goes to its safe
reaction starts within one iteration. No
rather than a majority, so the comparison
folds into channel b and the owner --
which is why this pattern is reachable in
Phase 4 while NVP is not. The name is
Koopman's; it is not IEC 61508 MooN
notation. Both channels always fire and
the token invalid; it never withholds it.
So the timing guarantee holds in the
degraded mode too (Q4), at the price of
being conservative in the fault-free case.
